new_statements.translation: In this paper we do not include a section on Malali prosody. We limit ourselves to speculating that stress was not contrastive and fell on the last syllable of the (phonological?) word, given that this is the case in the better-known languages of the Transanfranciscan family for which we have recordings and/or transcriptions made by trained linguists (Maxakali, Ritual Maxakali, Pataxo-Hahahae and Krenak). Added to this is the fact that most of the diacritic accents in the Malali records are on the last vowel of the word.

new_statements.rule_in_words: For 'Maxakali Ritual' (the Language of the Ritual Songs, which Nikulin 2020:18 and Nikulin & Silva 2020:7 equate with the 19th-c. Makuni complex incl. Martius's 'Macuni' = macu1258), the authors state from their own recordings/transcriptions that stress is non-contrastive and word-final. For Macuni as recorded in 1816-1818 (Wied, Saint-Hilaire, Eschwege) no author states a rule; Saint-Hilaire (1830 II:214 n.1) explicitly says he did not attend to accentuation, though the accents he did write on Macuni forms (II:48) are nearly all final (Tupá, tatán, atinán, etcoló, nhimcotó, canhá).
new_statements.domain_note: word (phonological word); statement made in passing in a paper on the sister language Malali, asserted for Maxakali Ritual as performed today by Maxakali speakers (Campos 2009:30-31 transcriptions of ritual-language words likewise all show final stress).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog macu1258 'Macuni' is the language of three 1816-1818 wordlists (Wied-Neuwied 1821 II:323-325 'Maconis'; Saint-Hilaire 1830 II:47-48 'Macunis', Alto dos Bois near Minas Novas; Eschwege), compiled by Martius 1867 II:173-176. Nikulin (2020:18) tags 'Maxakali Ritual [capo1236, macu1258]' and groups Macuni with Machacari/Capoxo/Cumanacho/Panhame as the 'Makuni' dialect complex, 'muito proximo ao Maxakali Ritual' (the Lingua dos Cantos Rituais still sung by Maxakali [maxa1247] speakers). The quoted stress statement is about Maxakali Ritual as recorded from modern Maxakali performers, not about the 19th-c. Macuni records themselves, for which no stress statement exists (Saint-Hilaire disclaims accent notation). Modern spoken Maxakali (maxa1247, already catalogued separately) also has final stress.

sources.note: p.8: states that in the better-known Transanfranciscan languages with recordings/transcriptions by trained linguists -- 'Maxakali, Maxakali Ritual, Pataxo-Hahahae e Krenak' -- stress is non-contrastive and falls on the last syllable of the word; uses this to speculate the same for Malali, adding that most diacritic accents in the 19th-c. Malali records sit on the final vowel. 'Maxakali Ritual' = the Makuni complex incl. Macuni per Nikulin 2020:18. Only explicit stress statement found that covers this languoid.

sources.note: sec. 2.2 pp.7-8: identifies the Lingua dos Cantos Rituais (LCR) with the 19th-c. lists 'Machacari, Machaculi, Machacali, Macuni, Capoxo, Cumanacho, Panhame' (Quadro 4 compares LCR with 'Macuni'); sets the 19th-c. data aside because of 'serias dificuldades relacionadas a fonologizacao'. p.48 (sec. 5.2): treats the last syllable as 'por consequencia, tonica' and person prefixes as 'desprovidos de acento dinamico' (proto-level assumption). No stress rule stated for Macuni/LCR as such.

sources.note: Primary collector. p.47: Macunis 'tirent les sons de leur gorge et parlent la bouche presque fermee'; p.48 n.1 'Je suis encore ici l'orthographe portugaise'. No stress rule; p.214 n.1 explicitly disclaims careful accent notation ('J'engage les voyageurs.. a s'occuper de l'accentuation plus soigneusement que je n'ai malheureusement songe a le faire'). His Macuni forms that do carry accent marks have them almost all on the final syllable (Tupá, tupabén, teoptatinán, atinán, tatán, etcoló, nhimcotó, canhá, haám, etpór) -- raw data only.
